items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: I can remember sitting in the Artie Shaw Band for the first time and opening the book and see that signature of Buddy Rich in there

ctx.x: They make you help with shuffleboard now, huh? Well can you tell me about, you said the Benny Goodman Big Band is coming up and I know you’ve done some of that in the past.

Yeah I was quite flattered. I can remember sitting in the Artie Shaw Band for the first time and opening the book and see that signature of Buddy Rich in there, and it hit me in a big way, that I had forgotten that he had sat in that chair. And the responsibility was, when Dick Johnson would announce that Buddy Rich was with the band and he used to solo, he used to change the tunes, “Lady Be Good,” there was a responsibility there I felt, to Buddy, to do the best I can. And I always like got plenty of rest, ate…

myself to death because I had a responsibility there. And with the Benny Goodman Band of course one of my favorite drummers, Gene Krupa was with that band, and I also feel a responsibility to that. I can remember playing, we did a sextet job, a small band with vibes and someone came up to me and they said, “Gene, you look great.” Because my initials are GC and they just assumed it was Gene Krupa.
